ENGLISH — MOCK EXAM #6
====

GRADE: Grade 7
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. A person, place, thing, or idea
   B. Only a describing word
   C. Only a joining word
   D. Only an action

2. When practising Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.

3. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.

4. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.

5. When practising Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks.

6. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

7. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. quickly
   B. happiness
   C. blue
   D. run

8. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.

9. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.

10. When practising Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives.

11. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library?
   B. Where is the Library
   C. Where is the library
   D. where is the library

12. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. One main idea with supporting sentences
   B. Many unrelated topics with no link
   C. Only one word repeated
   D. No full stops

13. When practising Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness.

14. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goes
   B. going
   C. went
   D. goed

15. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar In Use 9.3.1 Conjunctions and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 9.4.1 Intensive reading: Class Reader and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Narrative Composition 10.5.1 Packing and Shopping lists 11.5.1 Spelling Antonyms and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 9.5.1 Creative writing: Narrative compositions and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 10.1.1 Oral Presentations: Delivering Speeches and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Oral Presentations: Delivering Speeches and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 10.2.1 Study Skills: Note Making and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

23. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 10.3.1 Determiners and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
